turns.response_markdown: Tides are the regular rise and fall of ocean water caused mainly by the Moon’s gravity, with the Sun also contributing. As Earth rotates, coastal areas move through regions where water is pulled slightly higher or lower. Most places experience two high tides and two low tides each day. The timing and height of tides vary because of coastline shape, ocean depth, and the Moon’s position. Tides influence marine life, navigation, fishing, and coastal environments by moving large amounts of seawater in predictable natural cycles around the planet every day.
